source_text: I don't know what's meant by an empty pattern feedback file that sounds like, at best, a stopgap measure but it isn't something I asked to have created, and I don't understand what it's actually supposed to implement.

fragments.text: I don't know what's meant by an empty pattern feedback file that sounds like, at best, a stopgap measure but it isn't something I asked to have created, and I don't understand what it's actually supposed to implement.

reply_text:
㊥ ("it isn't something I asked to have created") You are right on both points: I found no request of yours behind this mechanism, and "start from an empty file" was housekeeping that I should not have put to you as a decision. I withdraw that question. Below is what the mechanism is and what I propose in its place.

🈖 ("what it's actually supposed to implement") It is meant to make the machine prefer patterns that worked before, across clicks. It works in two steps:
1. **After a click:** the machine appends one record to a file, listing the patterns in the chosen cascade and whether each is credited.
2. **Before the next selection:** it reads every record in the file and counts the credits per pattern. A candidate cascade that contains credited patterns has its habit weight multiplied up, so it is more likely to be chosen again.

The file is where those credits are kept between clicks. The fix you approved changed when a credit is given in step 1.

㊢ (where it came from) codex-10 added it on 1 October in four commits; one of them was dispatched by claude-17. I looked at the commit messages and at the notes under `futon2/holes` and `docs`, and found no ruling or note asking for it. I did not search further than that.

🈖 ("at best, a stopgap measure") The file currently holds seven records from 1–4 October, written before the machine measured wants at all. Five of them give credit, and the next selection will still count those. By "empty file" I meant setting those seven aside so the next click starts with no credits. That would only tidy the inputs of a mechanism whose place in the machine is itself undecided.

㊭ (in place of that question) Leave the mechanism and the file as they are for the next click, and use the click to show you the mechanism working on real values:
- which patterns were in each candidate cascade;
- what credit each pattern carried from the seven old records;
- how much that changed each candidate's habit weight;
- whether it changed which candidate was chosen;
- what record the click then wrote.

With that example in front of you, the decision is whether to keep the mechanism and specify it in Lean, or to take it out of the habit term.

🈸 (one decision) May codex-10 run one click now, stopped after selection and after the feedback record so those values can be read?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what changed) In `cascade_feedback.clj`:
- **Positive record:** now needs at least one selected want classed reached or progressed. With that, the records are the same as before.
- **No want moved:** each pattern gets the new neutral status. It is counted separately so it can be inspected, and the habit factor does not read that count.
- **Scope:** the condition is per run, not per pattern. If one want is reached, all four patterns of the cascade still get credit.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(tests) Two new tests use the selected action of the last click (four wants, four patterns) and build the want accounting with the real functions.
- **All four wants false, as that click measured:** four neutral records, factor 1.0.
- **One want true:** one "successful", three "supporting", factor above 1.
- **Old rule put back temporarily:** the first test fails on 8 assertions, so it does catch the earlier behaviour.
- **Run:** 14 tests, 87 assertions, 0 failures; lint and paren checks clean; receipt committed beside the test.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two things the examples will run into)
- **A failed want changes nothing the next selection reads.** The per-pattern trial records are written, but marked "held" and "record-only", and they update no parameter. Only the enactment count on the habit moves.
- **The existing feedback file predates want accounting.** `data/wm-pattern-feedback/events.edn` holds 7 events from 1–4 October, 5 of them with positive credit, and the next selection still reads them. By your ruling that the earlier implementation is not evidence, they should probably not feed the rebuilt machine. I have left the file alone.

("in the next click or two") Two decisions:
1. May codex-10 run one click now? If so, I will have it stopped after selection and after the feedback record so you can look at the values above.
2. Should the click start from an empty pattern-feedback file? I recommend yes, with the old file moved aside and kept, so the before-and-after counts in the example come only from this run.
